title: OECS Islands for Kids: Names, Flags, and Pride
excerpt: Children from the smaller Eastern Caribbean islands are often misnamed. Here are OECS places to say correctly, with one true detail each.
content:
Ask a child in the diaspora where their people are from, and listen for the correction: not Jamaica, not Trinidad. Antigua. Saint Lucia. Grenada. The smaller Eastern Caribbean islands have their own flags, foods, and names. OECS is the group many of those governments use to work together. You can teach the letters later. First, teach the place.

Say these places

This guide covers these OECS members:

  • Antigua and Barbuda — two islands, one country. The capital is St. John's, on Antigua. There is more than one island in the name, the same way Trinidad and Tobago works.
  • Dominica — often called the Nature Island. It is not the Dominican Republic. If a form, a teacher, or a cartoon mixes them up, correct it kindly and clearly.
  • Grenada — the Spice Island. Nutmeg is the famous one. A jar in the kitchen is a better lesson than a slogan.
  • Montserrat — a small island that lived through the Soufrière Hills volcano. Many families left and still call Montserrat home. Do not treat that as a fun explosion story. Follow the family's lead.
  • Saint Kitts and Nevis — two islands, one country. The official name is long. Children can practice both island names.
  • Saint Lucia — known for the Pitons, two volcanic peaks. The capital is Castries. Kwéyòl (Creole) is part of life for many families. If you speak it, use it.
  • Saint Vincent and the Grenadines — a main island plus many Grenadine islands. It is not Grenada, even though the words look related. Saint Vincent's capital is Kingstown.

Flags without a fake textbook

Each of these places has its own flag. Do not make a child memorize seven flags in one afternoon. Pick the family flag, look at a clear picture, and draw it. Later, add a neighbor. Island Hop and portal Flag Match are for another round of practice across the Caribbean. They will not know your grandmother's village. You will.

Island Passport Explorer, in the portal, is a place-and-play activity, not a citizenship exam.

Why the mix-up happens

Pop culture exports Jamaica and Trinidad more loudly. School units sometimes say "the Caribbean" and show one beach. Children from the OECS notice when their island is missing. The repair is specific: use the country name, learn one food, and refuse the joke that every accent is the same.

Barbados sits on the same map and is a separate country. It is not in this OECS list. See Barbados culture learning for kids. For life far from all of these islands, see teaching island pride in the diaspora.

faq.question: Which islands are in this OECS guide?
faq.answer: Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. These are OECS member countries and territories. This article does not try to list every associate member.

faq.question: Is Dominica the same as the Dominican Republic?
faq.answer: No. Dominica is an Eastern Caribbean island in the OECS. The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti and is a different country. The names sound alike. They are not the same place.

faq.question: Does Likkle Legends have a separate course for every OECS island?
faq.answer: No. Flag and place games cover the wider Caribbean. They are practice, not a full national curriculum. Family stories still do the specific teaching.
